a_existing_detector_only.reason: The semantic family is in the controlled taxonomy, but the current analyzer emitted no Selfdestruct finding on the exact deployed snapshot. The pinned source uses legacy suicide(_to), the AST compiler is fixed at solc 0.8.25 while the source requires 0.4.x, and the comparator matcher recognizes only selfdestruct(. The owned 0.8.25 vulnerable contrast is detected and comparator-confirmed, so the miss is an exact-source compatibility/implementation observation rather than a taxonomy gap.

owned_fixed_contrast.rationale: No detectors triggered. Source contains only a constructor and two functions that immediately revert; there are no occurrences of delegatecall or .delegatecall (so no DELEGATECALL Usage or Storage Collision), no selfdestruct or suicide keyword (so no Selfdestruct), no mint/burn logic or token transfers (so no Public Mint/Burn), no use of tx.origin (so no tx.origin Auth), no patterns of flash-loan vulnerable external calls or protocol interactions (so no Flash Loan Attack Vector), no low-level transfers (.call, .send, .transfer) or unchecked return handling (so no Unchecked Transfer), no for/while loops (so no Unbounded Loop), and no use of block.timestamp or now (so no block.timestamp Usage). The functions are marked pure/external and immediately revert, and state is set only in the constructor (immutable variables), which provides no evidence for the listed detectors.

owned_vulnerable_contrast.rationale: The source contains an explicit selfdestruct invocation: function kill(address payable recipient) external { require(owner[msg.sender], "not owner"); selfdestruct(recipient); } — the presence of the selfdestruct(...) call is the concrete pattern matched. No delegatecall, tx.origin, loops, block.timestamp usage, unchecked low-level transfer patterns, mint/burn functions, or reentrancy-typical external calls are present in the provided code.

pinned_source.rationale:
DELEGATECALL Usage (AST): multiple explicit delegatecall usages present: assembly delegatecall in Wallet constructor (assembly { ... delegatecall(...) }), and runtime delegatecall calls in Wallet fallback and in hasConfirmed/isOwner (e.g. _walletLibrary.delegatecall(msg.data)).

Selfdestruct: WalletLibrary.kill contains suicide(_to), i.e. explicit self-destruct opcode usage.

Reentrancy (AST): external call performed before critical state cleanup: in confirm(bytes32) the code does if (!m_txs[_h].to.call.value(m_txs[_h].value)(m_txs[_h].data)) throw; then later MultiTransact(...) and delete m_txs[_h]; state (m_txs) is deleted after the external call, introducing a reentrancy pattern.

Storage Collision (Delegatecall): WalletLibrary declares storage for mappings/arrays beyond the fields present in Wallet (e.g. mapping(bytes32 => PendingState) m_pending; bytes32[] m_pendingIndex; mapping(bytes32 => Transaction) m_txs; etc.), while Wallet has a shorter field list. The contract uses delegatecall into WalletLibrary (see fallback and constructor), meaning the library code will read/write the caller (Wallet) storage slots — a concrete pattern that can cause storage collisions.

block.timestamp Usage (AST): the code uses now in today(): function today() private constant returns (uint) { return now / 1 days; } (now is block.timestamp).
